text: To assuage a worry is to make it smaller and easier to bear. Officials pick each school's language one school at a time to calm people's fears.
To foster something is to help it grow and get stronger. Senegal wants to foster teaching in the languages children speak at home.
Indigenous means belonging to a place because it began there or has been there a very long time. Africa's indigenous languages come from Africa itself.
A lingua franca is a shared language people use when their home languages differ. Wolof plays that role in Dakar.
An official language is the one a government chooses for laws, offices and schools. In Senegal that is French, even though many children do not speak it well.
An initiative is a new plan started to fix a problem or reach a goal. This one began in 2021.
Surveyors are people who go out to look at something carefully and collect facts. These ones listened to what languages children used.
A mapping exercise means finding out and recording what is where. Here it means finding out which languages are spoken in which places.
Occasional means happening now and then, not all the time. A few French words popped up once in a while.
To throw in a word means to add it casually while talking. The children tossed in a French word here and there.
Transitioning means slowly changing from one thing to another. Children start in a local language and then move to another.
Constitutionally means according to the country's main set of laws, called the constitution. Six languages are named in it.
Recognised here means officially accepted as real and important. It is a British spelling of recognized.
Barely means only just, almost not at all. Many children can barely follow lessons in French.
Estimated means a careful guess, not an exact count. Nobody counted every child.
Here a share means a part of a whole group, like a slice of a pie. In Fatick that slice is 87%.
When one thing mirrors another, it looks just like it. Senegal's problem matches the rest of Africa.
A continent is one of Earth's giant land areas. Africa is one.
Fluent means able to speak or read a language easily and smoothly.
Formal instruction means lessons taught in a school by a teacher, not just picked up at home.
Insufficiently means not enough. A language that is insufficiently developed has not been practiced enough for school learning.
A basis is the base that other things are built on. A strong first language can be the base for learning a new one.
A researcher is someone whose job is to study a topic and find out facts.
Instruction means teaching. Local-language instruction means teaching in a local language.
To falter is to become weak or to stumble and not succeed. Earlier programs did not work well.
Funded means paid for with money. Big groups paid for the older programs.
Predominantly means mostly, or in the largest number. Villages that mostly speak Soninke will learn in Soninke.
Politically tricky means likely to cause arguments between groups of people. Favoring one language can upset others.
Wolofisation is the worry that Wolof will spread so much that other languages get pushed aside.
To crowd out something is to take up so much room that there is none left for it. Parents fear local languages will leave no room for French.
To dominate is to have the most power or control over something.
Colonial means linked to a time when one country ruled another. Former colonial powers are the countries that once ruled parts of Africa.
Essential means absolutely needed.
Gradual means happening a little at a time, not all at once.
To be anchored means held steady, like a boat with an anchor. Children should feel rooted in their own culture.
A ratio compares two amounts. Here it goes from 80 to 20 and then flips to 20 to 80.
Reverses means turns around the other way. The 80/20 split flips by age 12.
Wolof is a language spoken by many people in Senegal, especially in the capital, Dakar.
Pulaar is another language spoken in Senegal and nearby countries.
Dakar is the capital and biggest city of Senegal, on the Atlantic coast of West Africa.
Fatick is a mostly rural region in the south of Senegal.
Soninke is a language spoken in parts of Senegal and nearby countries.
USAID is the United States agency that gave money to help other countries.
